Accolades

  • For their work on this series Ann Nocenti earned a nomination for Eisner Award in 1989 in "Best Writer" category. John Romita Jr. and Al Williamson earned a nomination in "Best Penciller/Inker or Penciller/Inker Team" category.[1]

Notes

  • Although the cover title was Daredevil and the Black Widow from Daredevil #92 to Daredevil #107, the legal indicia continued to read as Daredevil only.
  • After Daredevil #233, Frank Miller agreed to write a two-part story for his old friend and colleague Walt Simonson. Millar wrote the first script, but never finished the story. An owner of a Daredevil fansite has the full script and even shared parts of it and story details.[2] This unpublished story was mentioned in Marvel Vision #12.
  1. ↑ 1989 Will Eisner Comic Industry Award Nominees HahnLibrary.net. Retrieved on January 10, 2025.
  2. ↑ Mithra, Kuljit Daredevil: The Lost Tales - Frank Miller/Walt Simonson Unpublished DAREDEVIL Script The Man Without Fear. Archived from the original on August 14, 2026. Originally retrieved on August 14, 2026.
